title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 183 (Who may employ agent)

content.overview: Section 183 provides that any person who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, may employ an agent.
content.glance: Any person of the age of majority (under the law to which he is subject) and of sound mind may employ an agent.
content.study: Section 183 provides that any person who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, may employ an agent. This is the statutory rule under Section 183 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Apply the elements stated in the text; do not extend beyond the provision. sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Any person who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, may employ an agent.

examples.title: Major and sound mind
examples.body: A person of majority age under the applicable law and of sound mind may employ an agent under Section 183.

hypotheticals.question: May a minor employ an agent?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 183 requires the person employing an agent to be of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and of sound mind.

examples: A major of sound mind may appoint an agent; a minor may not.
distinctions: Capacity of the principal (s. 183) differs from capacity of the agent (s. 184).

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 183
distinctions.body: Section 183 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.

misconceptions.myth: Section 183 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
